newsitem.title: USA: ARCO Chemical Q1 hurt by MTBE contracts end.
newsitem.headline: ARCO Chemical Q1 hurt by MTBE contracts end.

text.p: ARCO Chemical Co said Monday that the expiration of a number of fixed margin contracts on methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) was behind the lower net income it reported for the first quarter of 1997.
Alan Hirsig, president and chief executive officer, said the development was expected, adding "we had anticipated that 1997 would be a challenging year for ARCO Chemical."
The company said its earnings for the quarter declined to $48 million or $0.50 a share, from $106 million or $1.10 a share in the similar quarter in 1996.

At the same time, Hirsig said that during the first quarter, high raw material costs, coupled with weak product pricing, compressed margins in virtually all of the company's businesses. However, sales volumes were strong in the company's propylene oxide derivatives businesses, he said.

To mitigate profit fluctuations and give shareholders long-term value, Arco Chemical has taken several steps, he said, including tying to future compensation of executives to profit. In addition, executives will be required to own company stock at levels of one to four times base salary, he said.
The company is also implementing a broad scale program designed to increase efficiency and to achieve a very substantial reduction in structural costs, he said.
